scope.format: plain SQL (pg_dump default), one file per concern
scope.why_plain_not_custom: Plain SQL is greppable, diffable and restorable with psql alone. Custom format would need pg_restore and offers no benefit at this size.

included.expected_rows_note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from 52562. The published figure was an arithmetic error: the per-table list in legacy-control-totals.md section 1 sums to 53,742, not 52,562. 53,742 is the baseline total as of 2026-09-26.
included.actual_rows_note: The D1 backup holds 53,743 rows: 53,742 plus one row appended to settlement_runs (56 -> 57) by the nightly settlement cron between the 2026-09-26 baseline and the 2026-09-27 dump. Expected liveness, non-financial, and no financial control total moved.

auth_scope_decision.rationale: Auth UUID preservation is mandatory and uncorrectable after the fact, so these two tables must be captured. Sessions and refresh tokens carry live credential material with zero migration value, so including them would make the artefact more dangerous for no benefit.
auth_scope_decision.consequence: The artefact still contains auth.users.encrypted_password and MUST be treated as a secret-bearing file.

high_water_mark.status: AUTHORITATIVE MARK CAPTURED 2026-09-27 — see authoritative_mark. The reference_* fields below are the earlier 01:10 discovery capture, retained for comparison.
high_water_mark.reference_read_only_evidence: txid_current_if_assigned() returned null — the capturing statement was assigned no transaction id, so it wrote nothing

authoritative_mark.agreement_with_artefact: All ten counts in the mark match what the dump files actually contain. The mark was taken roughly one minute before the first dump began. This mutual agreement is the strongest available evidence that the artefact is a coherent point-in-time capture.
authoritative_mark.wallets_note: Later than the 2026-09-26 reference because the nightly 04:00 UTC recompute ran again. Count unchanged at 245.

high_water_mark.capture_method: Inside the same repeatable-read transaction pg_dump uses, run: select now(), plus per-table max(created_at)/max(updated_at). pg_dump does not emit this, so it is captured as a separate statement immediately before the dump begins and recorded in high-water-mark.json.
high_water_mark.observed_liveness: Counts were identical across three independent captures on 2026-09-26 and 2026-09-27 (~24.5 hours apart). Zero new rows in the core tables during that window. Production is live but currently low-volume. This is a measurement, not a guarantee.

control_totals_reference.note: Restore verification compares the restored copy against these. Amounts are integer kobo. naira-to-kobo conversion is exact: no value in the database exceeds 2 decimal places and none is negative.
control_totals_reference._deposits_label_correction_2026_09_27: The former key 'gross_kobo': 9002064126 sat beside 'success': 4260 and read as though it were the gross of the successful subset. It is not. 9,002,064,126 kobo is the gross of ALL 6,201 deposits; the successful 4,260 gross 6,042,365,363 kobo. Both figures were confirmed against the D1 backup on 2026-09-27. The key is now split so the two cannot be conflated during D2 restore verification. No source data changed.
control_totals_reference.known_drift_note: wallets.net_payment exceeds paid contributions by 359 kobo (NGN 3.59). This drift MUST reproduce in the restored copy — if it does not, the restore is not faithful.

method.tool: supabase db dump (CLI 2.109.1) or pg_dump 15 directly
method.read_only_detail: pg_dump issues only SELECT and takes ACCESS SHARE locks. It writes no data and changes no schema. It runs in a single repeatable-read transaction so the dump is internally consistent.
method.known_caveat: ACCESS SHARE conflicts with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. A concurrent ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE/VACUUM FULL would wait. Nothing in normal Kolekto operation issues those, and neither cron job does.

restore_instructions.gate: SEPARATE GATE — do not run in the same step as the backup
restore_instructions.why_not_local_dev_stack: It holds the new schema and uncommitted developer work, and `collections`/`profiles` exist in both with different shapes.

prerequisites_established_by_d1_verifica.extension_errors_are_expected: These five CREATE EXTENSION statements WILL error. No table, row, constraint or index depends on any of them. Enumerate the five in advance and tick them off; treat any error on CREATE TABLE, COPY, ADD CONSTRAINT or CREATE INDEX as real.
prerequisites_established_by_d1_verifica.roles_note: The dump carries 883 GRANT statements naming these roles. 'postgres' already exists as the container superuser. Create the four as 'nologin' stand-ins, one statement per role — a single DO block with one duplicate_object handler would swallow the first duplicate and skip the rest.
prerequisites_established_by_d1_verifica.psql_version_requirement: 15.14 or newer. pg_dump 15.19 wraps each file in \restrict / \unrestrict; an older psql fails at the top of the file. The postgres:15 image currently ships 15.19.
prerequisites_established_by_d1_verifica.restrict_tokens_are_not_secrets: The \restrict nonces are per-dump psql guard tokens, not credentials.
prerequisites_established_by_d1_verifica.cron_file_not_loadable_here: legacy-prod-cron.sql cannot be restored into this target because pg_cron is unavailable and the cron schema will not exist. Verify its 2 rows by reading the file.

steps: docker exec -i kolekto-legacy-restore createdb -U postgres legacy_restore
create the four stand-in roles FIRST — see prerequisites_established_by_d1_verification
psql ... -f legacy-prod-schema.sql   (WITHOUT ON_ERROR_STOP, then audit the error log against the five expected extension errors)
psql ... --set ON_ERROR_STOP=on -f legacy-prod-public-data.sql   (a COPY failure is never acceptable)
then compare every figure in control_totals_reference, including the 359-kobo drift
restore_instructions.pass_condition: Every control total reproduces, including the drift. Any mismatch means the backup is NOT verified.
